subject: CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
title: Balaam’s Donkey
overview: Numbers 22:1-6 and 20-34 tells how Balak wanted Balaam to curse Israel, and how Balaam's donkey saw the angel of the LORD and spoke. In this sub-strand you will retell that story, practise obedience to God, and learn to bless people instead of speaking ill of them.

lessons.title: Retelling the story of Balaam and his donkey
lessons.intro: Animals do not normally talk. In Numbers 22 the LORD opened a donkey's mouth. The donkey had seen a danger that the rider had not seen.
lessons.notes:
Read Numbers 22:1-6 and 20-34 in a group. Those are the verses for this story. Do not add events from chapters that you have not read.

### Balak's request (verses 1-6)
The Israelites were camped in the plains of Moab. Balak, the king of Moab, was afraid of them. He sent messengers to Balaam son of Beor and asked Balaam to put a curse on the people, because they were too powerful for him. Balak believed that the person Balaam blessed was blessed, and the person he cursed was cursed.

### The journey (verses 20-22)
God told Balaam that if the men had come to call him, he should go with them, but he must do only what God told him. Balaam saddled his donkey and went. God was angry when he went, and the angel of the LORD stood in the road to oppose him. Balaam was riding the donkey, and two servants were with him.

### Three times the donkey saved him (verses 23-27)
The donkey saw the angel standing with a drawn sword. Three times she tried to avoid him. She turned into a field. Then, on a narrow path between vineyard walls, she pressed Balaam's foot against the wall. Then, where there was no room to turn, she lay down. Each time Balaam beat her. The third time he beat her with his staff.

### Why the donkey talked (verses 28-34)
The LORD opened the donkey's mouth. She asked what she had done to be beaten three times. Balaam said she had made a fool of him, and that he would kill her if he had a sword. She asked whether she had ever acted like this before. He said no. Then the LORD opened Balaam's eyes. He saw the angel, bowed down, and said, "I have sinned." The angel said the path was reckless, and that he would have killed Balaam and spared the donkey if she had not turned aside.

The donkey talked because the LORD opened her mouth, so that Balaam would know the angel was blocking a reckless path.

keyWords.meaning: to call for harm on someone with words
to speak good from God over someone
the messenger of God who stood in Balaam's road with a drawn sword

activity.title: Read and role-play the story
materials: Pencil and paper or a digital device
steps: Role-play the story of Balaam's donkey: the angel, the donkey, and Balaam.
Use a digital device or a pencil to draw one scene, such as the donkey seeing the angel.
Answer the question: Why did the donkey talk?

practice.question: What did Balak ask Balaam to do?
practice.answer: To put a curse on the Israelites, because they were too powerful for him.

practice.question: Why did the donkey talk?
practice.answer: The LORD opened her mouth so Balaam would know the angel was blocking his reckless path.

practice.question: How many times did Balaam beat the donkey, and what did she do each time?
practice.answer: Three times. She turned into a field, pressed his foot against a wall, and then lay down.

summary: Balak asked Balaam to curse Israel.
The donkey saw the angel and turned aside three times while Balaam beat her.
The donkey spoke because the LORD opened her mouth.

lessons.title: Obeying God and those who lead us
objectives: Apply the story by obeying God's instructions.
List why it is important to obey God and seniors.
lessons.intro: God gave Balaam a clear limit: go, but do only what I tell you. Balaam still needed an angel and a donkey to stop him. Obedience is better than waiting to be blocked.
lessons.notes:
In Numbers 22:20 God said Balaam must do only what God told him. That is the heart of obedience. Obedience means doing what God says, in the way He says it, even when another person offers a reward for something else. Balak wanted a curse. God did not give Balaam freedom to say whatever Balak wanted.

### What Balaam did wrong
He beat the donkey instead of asking why a faithful animal had stopped. He was ready to kill her. He did not see the angel until God opened his eyes. Then he admitted, "I have sinned. I did not realise you were standing in the road to oppose me." Seeing late is poorer than obeying early.

### Obeying God today
God's instructions for children are in the Bible. You already know some of them: tell the truth, honour parents, forgive, and do not steal. When a friend asks you to do the opposite, choose God's instruction.

### Obeying seniors
Seniors are people placed over you, such as parents, guardians and teachers. Obey them when they tell you what is right. Their instructions often keep you safe: come home on time, do not talk to strangers, finish your work. List with a partner why this obedience matters:

- It honours God, who tells children to obey parents.
- It prevents harm.
- It shows humility, the opposite of Balaam's anger.
- It keeps peace at home and at school.

If a senior ever tells you to do a wrong or harmful act, that order is not from God. Say no and tell another trusted adult. True obedience to God comes first. Sing a song about obedience so the class remembers the lesson.

keyWords.meaning: to do what God or a rightful leader has said
a direction that tells you what to do
people placed over you, such as parents and teachers

activity.title: List reasons to obey
steps: In pairs, list the importance of obeying God and seniors.
Role-play Balaam beating the donkey, then role-play him saying, "I have sinned."
Each learner says one instruction from God that he or she will obey this week.
Sing a song related to obedience.

practice.question: What limit did God give Balaam in Numbers 22:20?
practice.answer: He was to do only what God told him.

practice.question: What did Balaam say when he finally saw the angel?
practice.answer: He said, "I have sinned," and that he had not realised the angel was standing in the road.

practice.question: Give two reasons to obey God and your seniors.
practice.answer: Any two: it honours God, it prevents harm, it shows humility, it keeps peace. If a senior commands harm, obey God first and tell a trusted adult.

summary: God told Balaam to do only what God said.
Balaam admitted he had sinned when his eyes were opened.
Obey God's word, and obey seniors when they command what is right.

lessons.title: Bless others and revere God's greatness
objectives: Explain why we should bless and not curse or speak ill of others.
Acknowledge God's greatness and treat animals with care.
lessons.intro: Balak wanted harmful words spoken over a whole people. God blocked that path. Christians learn to speak good of others and to stand in awe of the God who rules even a donkey's mouth.
lessons.notes:
Numbers 22:6 shows Balak asking for a curse so that he could defeat Israel. The rest of the reading shows God in control of the road, the angel, the donkey and Balaam's mouth. People do not have the right to call down harm with their words.

### Bless, do not curse
To speak ill of someone means to say bad, untrue or unkind things about them. To curse is to wish harm on them. The class discusses why we should bless instead:

- God is the judge. We are not.
- Unkind words spread and break friendships.
- A curse wishes pain. Love wishes good.
- Speaking well of others builds social cohesion, people living together in peace.
- You would not want a classmate to curse you. Do not do it to them.

Blessing can be simple. Say something true and kind. Pray that God will help the person. Refuse to join a gossip circle.

### God's greatness
God opened a donkey's mouth and a man's eyes. He stood in the road as the angel with a sword. Balaam had to bow. That is greatness. We revere God when we speak of Him with respect, obey His word, and refuse to treat Him as small. Acknowledge means to admit openly: God is greater than any king, including Balak, and greater than any person who thinks his words can control the world.

### The donkey and animal welfare
Balaam beat his donkey three times even though she had carried him faithfully and was saving his life. The angel spared the donkey and warned the man. We learn not to beat, starve or mock animals. They are God's creatures. If an animal stops or cries, find out why before you hit it. Kindness to animals is part of revering the Creator.

keyWords.meaning: to say unkind or harmful things about someone
to honour God's greatness with deep respect
treating animals with care and not with cruelty

activity.title: Discuss blessing rather than cursing
steps: Discuss why you should bless and not curse or speak ill of others, using Numbers 22:1-6 and 20-34.
Each learner says one kind sentence about a classmate.
Draw the donkey and the angel, and write one sentence about treating animals well.
Sing a song about God's greatness and obedience.

practice.question: What did Balak want Balaam's words to do to Israel?
practice.answer: He wanted Balaam to curse them so that he could defeat them.

practice.question: Why should you not speak ill of others?
practice.answer: God is the judge, unkind words break peace, and love speaks good rather than wishing harm.

practice.question: What does the beating of the donkey teach about animals?
practice.answer: We should not beat animals. The donkey was faithful and was saving Balaam, and the angel spared her.

summary: Do not curse or speak ill of others. Bless them instead.
God's greatness is seen when He opens the donkey's mouth and Balaam's eyes.
Treat animals with care, not with beating.

quiz.question: Who asked Balaam to curse Israel?
quiz.explanation: Numbers 22:1-6 says Balak sent messengers to ask for a curse.

quiz.question: Why did the donkey speak?
quiz.explanation: Numbers 22:28 says the LORD opened the donkey's mouth.

quiz.question: What was the donkey trying to avoid?
options: The angel of the LORD with a drawn sword
quiz.explanation: She saw the angel in the road and turned aside.

quiz.question: How many times did Balaam beat the donkey?
quiz.explanation: She was beaten when she turned aside, when she crushed his foot, and when she lay down.

quiz.question: God told Balaam to...
options: say whatever Balak paid him to say
do only what God told him
quiz.explanation: Numbers 22:20 limits Balaam to God's instructions.

quiz.question: When Balaam saw the angel he said...
A senior tells you to do what is right. You should...
quiz.explanation: Obeying rightful seniors is part of applying this story. Harmful orders are refused and reported.

quiz.question: Why should Christians bless and not curse others?
quiz.answer: Because love speaks good, God is the judge, and unkind words destroy peace.
quiz.explanation: The class discusses this from Balak's request for a curse.

quiz.question: Speaking ill of a classmate means...
options: saying unkind or harmful things about them
quiz.explanation: Speaking ill is the opposite of blessing.

quiz.question: God's greatness in this story is seen when...
options: the LORD opens the donkey's mouth and Balaam's eyes
quiz.explanation: Only God could open the mouth and the eyes. That is why we revere Him.
